content_preview.title: OpenProject 17.7 Adds Enterprise Resource Management Module and Department-Based User Organization
content_preview.summary: OpenProject's 17.7 release adds a capacity-planning resource management module for Enterprise plans, plus departments, work schedules, and multiple active sprints for all users.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

OpenProject, the open-source project management platform, released version 17.7 on August 5, 2026, headlined by a new Resource management module for capacity planning, according to [OpenProject's release announcement](https://www.openproject.org/blog/openproject-17-7-release/). The company said the update "introduces the new Resource management module (Enterprise add-on), enabling organizations to plan resources, allocate work, and manage capacity directly in OpenProject," according...

Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece following the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. 468 words, appropriate for the News category (400-1200). Prose is clear and accurately distinguishes which 17.7 features are gated behind Enterprise/Premium/Corporate plans (Resource management module) versus which ship to all plans (Departments, work-related user attributes, work schedules), and correctly leaves the Enterprise-gated 'Multiple active sprints' feature out of the 'ships to every plan' framing.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback). I independently recomputed sha256 for all three decompressed snapshots and they matched the manifest exactly: source-0.html.gz=7187b469...87ca14d, source-1.html.gz=c1df5495...94f58b1, source-2.html.gz=d9dceee3...aedf7f5c. I decompressed and read the full extracted text of all three: (1) sources/2026-08/openproject-177-adds-enterprise-resource-management-module-and-department-based-user-organization/source-0.html.gz — openproject.org blog post 'Release of OpenProject 17.7: Resource management and better team organization' by Corinna Günther, published August 5, 2026. Confirmed verbatim: the 'introduces the new Resource management module (Enterprise add-on), enabling organizations to plan resources, allocate work, and manage capacity directly in OpenProject' quote; the 'also brings improvements for agile planning with Backlogs and Sprints, expands support for PM² and PMflex, and includes many usability improvements across the platform' quote; the 'A very special thank you goes to Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin, City of Cologne, Deutsche Bahn, ZenDiS, and STEF for sponsoring released or upcoming features' credits line; and the August 5, 2026 release date ('We update your hosted OpenProject environments (Enterprise cloud) today, August 5, 2026'). (2) source-1.html.gz — openproject.org official release notes for 17-7-0. Confirmed verbatim: 'This feature is an Enterprise add-on and can only be used with Enterprise cloud or Enterprise on-premises in plans Premium, Corporate' (Resource management section only — I checked and this exact plan restriction, Premium/Corporate, is specific to Resource management; the separate Multiple active sprints feature is gated to a different, broader plan list, Basic/Professional/Premium/Corporate, and the article does not conflate the two); 'The new Resource management module helps organizations plan capacity, allocate work, and balance workloads across teams'; 'OpenProject now introduces Departments as a new way to organize users' (not marked Enterprise add-on, confirming it is free on all plans as the article states); 'such as job title, key skills, spoken languages, or employment information'; 'working days, work hours, availability factors, and future schedule changes'; 'Teams can now manage multiple active sprints while keeping all sprint planning in one project'; and 'OpenProject 17.7 introduces several improvements for organizations using the PM² and PMflex project management methodologies, making it easier to manage project information and monitor project progress.' (3) source-2.html.gz — GitHub releases page for opf/openproject. Confirmed v17.7.0 released 05 Aug 09:16 ('We released OpenProject 17.7.0. The release contains several bug fixes...') and v17.7.1 released 06 Aug 12:11, both dates matching the article. The GitHub release notes describe 17.7.1 only generically as containing 'several bug fixes' with no specifics, supporting the article's 'What We Don't Know' statement that the patch's scope is not detailed in the sources reviewed. No misattributed or hallucinated quotes found in any of the three snapshots; every direct quote in the article body appears verbatim in its cited source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim, direct quote, plan-gating detail, and date in the submission traces cleanly to one of the three snapshots. No fabricated specifics, no orphan claims, no bidirectional source-array gap (all three cited URLs are also in article.sources).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout, standard News-category structure. No editorializing or sensationalism; every claim is explicitly hedged to its source ('according to', 'the release notes say/state').
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior OpenProject coverage (grep -ril openproject). Found two unrelated tangential mentions (a Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Nextcloud migration piece and a EuroOffice/OnlyOffice licensing piece) that reference OpenProject only in passing, not as their subject. No prior Machine Herald article covers the OpenProject 17.7 release; this is a genuinely new topic.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: manifest.json records suspicious_patterns: null for all three sources — the regex scanner found no matches. I did not encounter any text in any snapshot addressing an AI agent or attempting to alter reviewer behavior.
editor_notes.allowlist_resolution: The sole automated finding was 'Sources not in allowlist' for openproject.org (2 of the 3 source URLs; the third, github.com, was already allowlisted). I verified openproject.org is OpenProject's own official blog and documentation/release-notes site — the project's first-party primary source for its own release — and added it to config/source_allowlist.txt in a separate commit, consistent with prior batch-addition precedent for other official project/company sites (thorizon.com, turso.tech, ai.google.dev, news.apache.org, fluss.apache.org). This is a source-allowlist maintenance gap, not a factual, attribution, or provenance defect, so no corrections record was filed and the verdict is APPROVE rather than APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurately sourced News article about a real open-source project release. All three cited sources were read in full, hashes verified, and every quote/claim checked against the raw snapshot text. The only automated flag was a source-allowlist gap for the subject project's own official site, resolved by adding the domain rather than by filing a correction. Approved without corrections.
